jobs.title: FP&A Intern
jobs.description:

Cleveland-Cliffs Tooling and Stamping, has an immediate opportunity for a Automotive Program Manager in our Windsor, Ontario Stamping Facilities. jobs.title: Program Manager Environmental Permitting & Regulatory
jobs.description:
Location: Forbes, MN

Cleveland-Cliffs is seeking a highly experienced Program Manager Environmental Permitting & Regulatory to lead environmental permitting and regulatory initiatives for our Mining and Pelletizing operations in Northern Minnesota and the Upper Peninsula of Michigan. The Program Manager will manage aspects of environmental permitting and closely coordinate with site environmental managers, including providing guidance and overseeing the preparation of environmental permit applications.  The Program Manager will also monitor and analyze emerging environmental regulations for their impact on the business, engage in state and federal environmental rulemaking, and advocate for sound environmental regulatory policy development with external stakeholders and trade associations. This position will report to the Environmental Director for our Mining and Pelletizing business.  The position will either be located in Northeastern Minnesota (at United Taconite Forbes office) or at the company headquarters in Cleveland, Ohio.

Summary of Responsibilities:
- Oversee environmental permit application and ensure consistency amongst sites.  Primary permitting oversight activities include: Wetlands (Section 404/ Army Corps of Engineers and Wetlands Conservation Act/Minnesota DNR), Permit to Mine (Minnesota DNR), etc.

- Develop procedures and ensure consistency amongst sites for carrying out reclamation activities; tracking and updating financial assurance obligations; tracking environmental performance, etc.

- Assist in developing proactive NPDES/State Disposal System water permitting/reissuance strategies to address evolving regulations and Waters of the United States/Waters of the State definitions.

- Monitor and analyze emerging environmental regulations and laws at the local, state, and federal levels, assess their impact on the company's operations, and provide guidance to the site environmental Managers.

- Advise the Environmental Director and maintain risk registries to address emerging regulations, permitting issues, operational risks, and compliance obligations.

- Conduct site environmental assessments and identify potential environmental risks and liabilities.

- Evaluate prospective projects against environmental review obligations (NEPA/MEPA) and manage EAW/EIS studies, if required.

- Develop and maintain positive relationships with multiple stakeholders, including internal teams, regulatory agencies, and local communities. Represent the company on industry trade association environmental committees.

- Advise the Environmental Director on opportunities and priorities on advocating for improvements to environmental legislation or regulations.  Develop comments and engage with local, state, and federal agencies on environmental rulemaking and policy development.

- Additional responsibilities as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:
- Bachelor’s degree in engineering or environmental discipline.

- Familiarity with design and operation of air emission control and water treatment systems for the industrial sector.

- Demonstrated experience in preparing and submitting environmental permit applications and other environmental compliance requirements/reports/documentation.

- Expertise in analyzing and interpreting the environmental regulations' impact on facilities.

- Applicants for this position must be currently legally authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.

Preferred Qualifications :
- Minimum of 10 years of professional environmental experience, including permitting and reporting.

- Expertise in analyzing and interpreting the environmental regulations' impact on facilities.

- Working knowledge of the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act (Section 401, 402, 404), Minnesota/Michigan air quality regulations.

The salary range for this role is $110,000 - $140,000.  An employee’s pay within the salary range will be based on numerous factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, experience, skills, geographic location, and business or organizational needs.

Cleveland‑Cliffs is seeking a Process Manager for the Roll Shop at our New Carlisle, IN facility, a 24/7 steel manufacturing operation producing cold‑rolled, hot‑dipped galvanized, galvannealed, and electrogalvanized steel coils. This leader oversees daily roll shop activities supporting rolling operations, roll maintenance, roll changes, and roll performance optimization. The role is responsible for safe operations, equipment reliability, workforce leadership, and continuous improvement within a critical support area of the plant. Ideal candidates bring strong manufacturing leadership, hands‑on technical problem‑solving skills, and experience in roll shop or rolling mill environments.

Summary of Responsibilities:

- Leads and coaches roll shop personnel to achieve safety, quality, and production performance targets.
- Ensures full compliance with safety standards, environmental regulations, and plant operating procedures; takes immediate action to correct unsafe conditions.
- Oversees roll shop workflows including roll inspection, grinding, maintenance, changeouts, and preparation for rolling operations.
- Drives continuous improvement, lean manufacturing initiatives, and process optimization within the roll shop and related support functions.
- Coordinates daily activities with operations, maintenance, engineering, and production planning to ensure roll availability and equipment reliability.
- Provides coaching and counseling on safety, attendance, work rules, and interpretation of USW Collective Bargaining Agreement language.
- Tracks key performance indicators (roll performance, downtime, maintenance metrics, overtime, absenteeism) and implements corrective actions.
- Facilitates team meetings and ensures consistent communication on safety, environmental, quality, training, and budget topics.
- Identifies skill gaps and leads training in roll shop techniques, equipment operation, quality systems, and maintenance practices.
- Partners with Equipment Control maintenance teams to address equipment deficiencies, improve reliability, and support root‑cause analysis.
- Maintains strong shop‑floor presence and provides operational support based on business needs.
- Participates in facility and vendor project teams to improve roll performance, reduce costs, and enhance operational reliability.
- Coordinates with outside processing vendors to meet roll shop and production requirements.
- Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

- High school diploma or equivalent.
- Leadership experience in manufacturing, industrial operations, or maintenance environments.
- Effective communication skills across all organizational levels.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Outlook, advanced Excel, PowerPoint).
- Experience using a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS).
- Ability to work effectively in a fast‑paced steel production environment.

- Ability to work in a plant environment with exposure to heat, noise, and moving equipment.
- Ability to walk long distances, climb stairs, and access elevated or confined areas.
- Must support a 24/7 operation, including off‑shift availability as needed.
- Minimal travel for training or vendor coordination.

- Applicants for this position must be currently legally authorized to work in the United States on a full‑time basis.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations, or a related technical/business field.
- 3+ years of experience leading a manufacturing operations or maintenance team.
- Experience working in a unionized environment.
- Roll shop experience supporting roll grinding, roll maintenance, roll changeouts, or rolling mill operations.
- Experience with continuous improvement, lean manufacturing, and problem‑solving methodologies.
- Strong understanding of rolling mill processes, roll performance, and equipment reliability.

jobs.title: Shift Manager Operations
jobs.description:
Location: Babbitt, MN

Cleveland-Cliffs has an immediate opening for a Shift Manager Railroad Operations at our Northshore Mining Company facility located in Babbitt, MN. The primary responsibility of this position of the Shift Manager Railroad Operations is to direct and monitor Railroad Operations crews with effective leadership to safely execute the work set in the Railroad Operating and Maintenance of Way plans. The Shift Manager must be willing to work with all departments to prioritize safe production, monitor and correct any quality or environmental issues, and ensure all employees’ adherence to company policies. The Shift Manager will be required to maintain safety as a top priority throughout the day and when contacted after hours, effectively communicate with all employees, and demonstrate consistent leadership.

Summary of Responsibilities:
- Create and promote a positive working atmosphere in order to safely and efficiently execute the goals of the railroad operating and maintenance plan.
- Continually monitor technicians for adherence to safety standards and the RR operating rulebook through performance of assigned tasks
- Previous supervisory experience.
- Communicate to all crew members their job assignments, timing expectations, and associated tasks.  Follow-up on progress throughout the shift.
- Conduct safety and informational meetings to crew and complete safety contacts in the field
- Coach, direct, and develop technicians on tasks completed in the RR department.
- Consistently follow-up on any safety concerns.
- Take proactive measures to correct any safety or production problems that arise.
- Communicate with Railroad Dispatcher, Mine Dispatcher, Railroad maintenance technicians, coarse crusher, and the Silver Bay Railroad Shift Manager to meet the production goals set forth by the train schedule and maintenance schedule.
- Manage training needs and promotions for department personnel.
- Manage the daily train schedule to achieve inventory necessary for successful pellet production.  This may also require management on the off-shift.
- Coordinate the response to emergencies utilizing the resources available
- Be available to respond to derailments or other threats to production.
- Oversee contractors involved in railroad maintenance of way projects and any contractor performing work within the railroad right of way.
- Complete and submit all necessary safety, environmental, and production reports within the required timeframe.
- Ensure work order discipline is adhered to and work completion documentation is maintained.
- Manage weekly personnel schedule and yearly vacation schedule to ensure proper staffing levels for required activities.
- Developing portions of the track maintenance program.  This will include (but not limited to) contractor management, project development, material ordering and maintenance component inventory management.
- Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:
- Minimum of 5 years’ experience in mining or heavy industry, with preference given to those with railroad operations or railroad maintenance experience.
- Must be willing to work a rotating dayshift schedule including weekends.
- Must be a champion of safe production methods and ideals.  Promote continuous improvement.  Must understand and be able to communicate and implement company safety rules, MSHA standards, environmental policies and procedures, and quality standards.
- Previous successful leadership experience is required.
- Must understand the broader vision of the job function, company organization, and the mining industry.
- Must have the ability to plan, coordinate and follow-up on multiple work tasks with a variety of employees, departments, and contractors.  Must be able to set clear goals and develop strategies to meet these goals.
- Must have excellent communication skills.  Must be able to clearly communicate the shift operating plan to employees and interact with other departments to meet the goals of the operating plan.
- Must be able to think logically using factual data provided.  Must be able to make decisions based on information provided and input from others.  Must be able apply knowledge of safety rules, RR operating rules, and other company policies to guide the decision-making process.
- Clearly communicate and implement all new policies introduced and be able to provide technicians with up-to-date information regarding current best practices and standards.
- Must have strong computer skills and be proficient in Microsoft Office Software

Preferred Qualifications:

jobs.description:
Location: Hibbing, MN

Cleveland-Cliffs has an immediate opening for a Shift Manager Operations at Hibbing Taconite Company in Hibbing, MN. As a Shift Manager, you will direct and coordinate safe production at the Mine. Supervise the efforts of experienced operators and technicians to safely and efficiently perform their tasks.  The Shift Manager will lead mine operations crew and shift maintenance resources to safely meet performance expectations.

Summary of Responsibilities :
- Coordinate, facilitate, and motivate employees to safely and efficiently execute and complete their work assignments.

- Strive to keep all employees safe and achieve this by training in safe work practices.

- Complete planned inspections, safety contacts, and task observations as part of the safe production focus.

- Establish high-performance standards for the employees, promote and encourage the achievement of these standards, provide feedback to employees on their progress, and implement disciplinary measures if necessary.

- Update scheduling personnel on daily and weekly carry-over work.

- Supervise hourly employees’ work and develop an understanding of the work being done to increase skill level and maximize operating efficiency.

- Ensure employee compliance with corporate, property, and departmental policies and standard work procedures. Ensure compliance with the collective bargaining agreement.

- Coordinate and facilitate departmental training needs and encourage and assist in employee development.

- Analyze and evaluate the work of technicians and operators with an emphasis on producing recommendations necessary to drive continuous improvement in mine operations.

- Coordinate and facilitate employee involvement in the ongoing improvement of work practices and procedures.

- Communicates and implements safety and loss control standards, company safety rules, and MSHA regulations. Understands and communicates environmental policies and procedures.

- Resolve employee problems through effective communication.

- Communicate with the Mine dispatch operator as it relates to the delivery of ore to the Plant to prevent disruptions in either the Mine or Plant. When issues arise and disruption is evident, take the immediate corrective actions required and provide information to the senior supervisor identifying the issue and the corrective action taken.  If corrective actions cannot be immediately addressed, elevate the issue through the action card process whereby it can be reported on in the level two meeting and the section manager can make the task assignment to address the action card.

- Supervise and direct operating crews and hold them accountable to safely meet performance expectations and standard work.  Where there is variation to the standard work being performed between crews or individuals take the necessary action to educate to standards.  In the event the standard needs to be modified by identifying improvements to the standard, document the recommended change to the standard and bringing the improvement opportunity to the senior supervisor for review.

- Implement and sustain current best practices related to maximizing production to minimize variation across crews.  Where variation is present, review the standards with the individuals and monitor the standard which will minimize variation.

- Monitor Mine performance during the shift to ensure the process operates within the operating parameters and address variation to minimize process disruptions.  In the event, the process falls outside of the operating parameters, take corrective actions.  If unable to return the process to within the parameters, elevate the issue to the senior supervisor, identify the current issue, and what actions were tried (or not) to attempt to bring the process back into the operating parameters.

- When equipment deficiencies create an immediate disruption to the process, take immediate corrective action utilizing the proper crafts available.  If the deficiency is not creating an immediate operating disruption, enter quality work orders into the system as defined by the standard.  At a minimum, the work order identifies the equipment, contains a brief explanation of the issue, the physical location of the deficiency, includes the originator's priority, and as much additional information that can be attained to assist the Maintenance Department.

- Monitor and maintain environmental compliance in the Mine and take the proper actions when required such as dust collection, spill reporting, and fugitive dust.  While on shift, the operations supervisor is the single point of accountability for environmental compliance.  Understand the department’s environmental compliance requirements and work directly with the Environmental Department for direction, responsibilities, and accountabilities that support environmental compliance.

- Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:
- 2-year degree in technical field or equivalent.

- 3-5 years’ recent experience at a mining/mineral processing facility or heavy industry, preferably in a unionized environment.

- Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills such as team building and conflict resolution are required. Willingness to promote team concepts and company policies. Ability to motivate, delegate, establish, and work in a collaborative environment.

Must be able to work rotating shifts, weekends, and holidays, to ensure 24-hour coverage, 7 days per week. Regular attendance is an essential requirement. Must be able to physically perform all these responsibilities safely: walk on uneven surfaces, climb equipment, operate pickup, and other small fleet vehicles, etc.

The salary range for this role is $80,000 to $105,000.  An employee’s pay within the salary range will be based on numerous factors including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, experience, skills, geographic location and business or organizational needs.

Cleveland-Cliffs Steel LLC has immediate openings for Shift Manager Operations positions at our Cleveland, OH plant. The Shift Manager serves as a key link between hourly personnel, maintenance, and leadership to ensure safe, efficient, and reliable operations in a 24/7 manufacturing environment.

jobs.title: Shift Manager Operations
jobs.description:
Location: Toledo, OH

Cleveland-Cliffs has an immediate opportunity for a Shift Manager Operations at our Toledo, OH HBI location.  The Shift Manager Operations is responsible for the safe operation of the facility.  This position prioritizes, assigns, directs, and reviews work of Plant Operators and the control room based on standard work, and process conditions across the facility.  The role actively participates with all site personnel on shift to optimize plant production.

Summary of Responsibilities:
- Demonstrate safe work practices and lead work safely.

- Gather information from previous supervisor(s) and crew and use information to create a shift plan.

- Plan and prioritize work assignments from the weekly work order packet on a daily basis.

- Perform shift toolbox huddle, communicating shift plan, task assignments, shift operating parameters, and any special tasks required.

- Monitor and inspect the quality of completed work assignments.

- Complete shift inspection of crew member areas, inspecting the quality and completeness of work assignments.

- Write and close out work orders for crew, ensuring job hours are accurately reflected to tasks assigned.

- Ensure start and stop times are accurately reflected for payroll.

- Document shift performance for crew, work achieved, and key process parameters for handover to other operating personnel.

- Understand significant deviations from the department’s operating plan and make changes to correct and implement sustainable solutions to deviations.

- Elevate deviations to the manager that cannot be corrected at supervisor level.

- Collaborate with other supervisors to minimize variation between shifts and implement best practices.

- Administer corporate, site, and departmental policies consistently and impartially.

- Ensure incoming oxide and outgoing products are unloaded and loaded as efficiently as possible.

- Make recommendations on quality improvement initiatives, communicate the priority of process improvement work to subordinates, and monitor that the process improvement work is completed.

- Coordinate plans, projects, and programs to achieve the desired performance results in safety, quality, production, cost, and environmental performance.

- Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications :
- Associate Degree in business or related field.  May consider equivalent experience.

- 3-5 years of experience in heavy industrial environment preferably steel, hydrocarbon or mining environment.

- Experience overseeing, leading, and coaching people.

- Microsoft Office experience (Excel, Word, etc.)

- Ability to work under minimal supervision and effectively manage multiple/changing priorities.

- Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) experience; Ellipse preferred.

- Understanding of piping and instrumentation diagrams and single line diagrams for process isolation purposes.

- Reasonable mechanical aptitude (preferably with experience in pipe materials, specifications, fittings, seals, water piping/pumping systems, compressible fluid piping/pumping systems, welding, conveying equipment, gearing/bearings/power transmission).

- Effectively communicate both orally and through written text.

- Ability to read and constructively influence personnel in team processes.

- Ability to work under minimal supervision and effectively manage multiple/changing priorities.

- Occasionally lifting up to 25lbs.

- Mobility required.  Must be able to handle stairs and long periods of work on your feet.

- Routinely exposed to plant environment including noise, dust, dirt and vibrations, extreme climate changes / changes in weather.

- Ability to work at heights.

- Willing to work shift work.

- Applicants for this position must be currently legally authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.
